title: Roots: The Saga of an American Family
author: Alex Haley
description: The seven-generation journey of Kunta Kinte and his descendants from 18th-century Gambia through American chattel slavery to freedom, based solely on the novel by Alex Haley.

characters.archetypeTag: Lead · Male · Adult · Mandinka Warrior & Clan Ancestor
characters.overviewBio: Born in the village of Juffure, The Gambia, around 1750 to Omoro and Binta Kinte, Kunta is raised in the proud Islamic traditions and warrior discipline of the Mandinka people. At age seventeen, while venturing into the woods to find wood to carve a drum for his younger brother, he is ambushed and captured by toubob slave catchers. Survived the catastrophic Middle Passage aboard the slave ship Lord Ligonier, Kunta is sold in Annapolis to Virginia planter John Waller, who forces upon him the name 'Toby'. Fiercely refusing to accept enslavement, Kunta escapes four times; after the fourth attempt, professional slave catchers corner him and ruthlessly chop off the front half of his right foot with an ax. Sold to Dr. William Waller, he becomes his carriage driver, later marrying the cook Bell and fathering Kizzy. Kunta painstakingly teaches Kizzy the Mandinka words of his ancestors ('ko' for guitar, 'kamby bolongo' for the river), initiating the oral tradition that preserves the family's identity across two centuries.
characters.historicalNotes: The unyielding patriarch whose African pride, memory of Juffure, and refusal to surrender his birth identity anchor the entire novel.
quotes: A man is not a man if he does not know who his ancestors are.
Kunta Kinte was born in the spring of 1750 in the village of Juffure, four days' journey upriver from the coast of The Gambia.
The river is the Kamby Bolongo. A guitar is a ko.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Adult · Mandinka Elder & Father
characters.overviewBio: Kunta Kinte's father and an honored elder of the Kinte clan in Juffure. A quiet, revered blacksmith and devout Muslim, Omoro conducts the sacred eighth-day naming ritual beneath the starry sky, whispering Kunta's name into his ear so he would be the first to know who he was. Omoro guides Kunta through his manhood training (kafo), teaching him hunting, discipline, and tribal history.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Female · Adult · Loving Mother & Village Anchor
characters.overviewBio: Kunta Kinte's devoted mother in Juffure. Her melodic voice, protective maternal care, and stories of the ancestors define Kunta's earliest memories. When Kunta is captured by slave raiders, Binta is left grieving in Africa, unaware of her firstborn son's fate across the ocean.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Adult · First Slave Master
characters.overviewBio: A tobacco planter in Spotsylvania County, Virginia. John Waller purchases the seventeen-year-old Kunta Kinte at the Annapolis auction dock in 1767 for a bargain price due to the youth's rebellious demeanor, christening him 'Toby' and setting him to work clearing brush and building fences. Enraged by Kunta's repeated runaways that cost him substantial recovery fees, John Waller permits two brutal slave catchers to punish Kunta by chopping off his right foot rather than castrating him.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Adult · Second Slave Master / Physician
characters.overviewBio: John Waller's older brother, a prosperous country doctor and plantation owner in Spotsylvania County. Furious with his brother for economically ruining a prime worker through maiming, Dr. Waller buys Kunta, amputates the gangrenous bone properly, nurses him back to health, and appoints him his personal buggy driver. While presenting himself as more gentlemanly and rational than his brother, Dr. Waller exhibits absolute cruelty when he discovers sixteen-year-old Kizzy forged a pass for Noah, instantly selling her down south to Tom Lea with zero remorse despite Bell's desperate begging.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Elder · Plantations Mentor & Musician
characters.overviewBio: An elderly, gifted enslaved violinist on the Waller plantation who plays for white aristocratic balls as well as slave quarters dances. Assigned to look after the rebellious 'African', Fiddler teaches Kunta English and the harsh realities of plantation survival. He stays by Kunta's side after his foot is severed, dressing his wounds and acting as his truest friend and spiritual brother until his death.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Female · Adult · Head Cook & Kunta's Wife
characters.overviewBio: Dr. William Waller's proud, capable head cook at the Big House. Born into Virginia slavery, Bell has suffered the agonizing sale of two infant children from a previous union. Initially skeptical of the sullen, African buggy driver, she warms to Kunta's solemn dignity. They marry jumping the broom, and she gives birth to Kizzy. When Dr. Waller abruptly sells Kizzy away, Bell's spirit is crushed, leaving her and Kunta in inconsolable mourning.

characters.archetypeTag: Lead · Female · Adult · Cultural Keeper & Resilient Mother
characters.overviewBio: Daughter of Kunta Kinte and Bell, named from the Mandinka word meaning 'to stay put'. Secretly taught to read and write by the master's young niece Missy Anne, Kizzy uses her literacy to forge a travel pass for her enslaved sweetheart Noah. When Noah is captured, Dr. Waller traces the writing to Kizzy and summarily sells her to North Carolina cockfighter Tom Lea. Raped by Lea upon arrival, she gives birth to George. Despite profound isolation in North Carolina, Kizzy fiercely preserves her father's memories, teaching George about his grandfather Kunta Kinte, Juffure, and the African words.
characters.historicalNotes: The indispensable linchpin of the family's survival, carrying the oral torch across the devastating divide of the slave trade.

characters.archetypeTag: Minor · Male · Young Adult · Enslaved First Love
characters.overviewBio: A handsome young field hand on the Waller plantation with whom Kizzy falls in love. Longing for freedom up north, he persuades Kizzy to forge a travel pass for him. Caught by slave patrollers, his captured pass leads directly to Kizzy's discovery and tragic sale.

characters.archetypeTag: Lead · Male · Adult · Third Slave Master / Cockfighter
characters.overviewBio: A crude, insecure, and ambitious small-plantation owner in Caswell County, North Carolina, whose single obsessive passion is breeding and betting on fighting gamecocks. He buys sixteen-year-old Kizzy at auction in Richmond, rapes her on his wagon journey home, and fathers George. Recognizing young George's natural gift with fowl, Lea makes him his head gamecock trainer ('Chicken George'). Despite boasting of his paternal favor and promising George his manumission papers, Lea ruins himself in a high-stakes cockfight against an English lord and cowardly signs Chicken George over to the Englishman to satisfy his debts.
characters.historicalNotes: Exemplifies the cruel hypocrisy and economic instability of the southern slaveholding class.

characters.archetypeTag: Lead · Male · Adult/Elder · Master Gamecocker & Legend
characters.overviewBio: Son of Kizzy and Tom Lea, born into North Carolina slavery. Charismatic, flamboyant, green-eyed, and brilliantly skilled with birds, he rises to legendary status throughout the South as the premier gamecock handler. Married to Matilda, with whom he fathers eight children, George works tirelessly believing Tom Lea will grant his freedom. Instead, he is exiled to England for years as cockfight collateral. Returning to North Carolina on the eve of the Civil War as a free man, he helps shepherd his extended family through emancipation and the dangerous rise of night riders.
quotes: A slave's got to strut or he'll die crawling.
My granddaddy was an African named Kunta Kinte, from a place called Juffure!

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Female · Adult · Devout Matriarch & Field Preacher's Daughter
characters.overviewBio: Daughter of an enslaved preacher on a neighboring plantation, Matilda becomes Chicken George's steadfast wife. Deeply religious, stoic, and dignified, she anchors the family through decades of turmoil, raising their eight children during George's prolonged absence in England. She guides the clan under their subsequent master, Massa Murray, until emancipation.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Adult · Fourth Slave Master / Alamance Planter
characters.overviewBio: A wealthy planter in Alamance County, North Carolina. Following Tom Lea's financial collapse and the exile of Chicken George to England, Murray purchases Matilda and all of George's children and grandchildren. Murray keeps the family together on his plantation through the grueling years of the Civil War until Union victory dissolves the institution of slavery.

characters.archetypeTag: Lead · Male · Adult · Blacksmith Patriarch & Reconstruction Leader
characters.overviewBio: Fourth son of Chicken George and Matilda, and great-grandson of Kunta Kinte. Apprentices as a master blacksmith on the Murray plantation, known for his formidable physical strength, absolute integrity, and quiet defiance. Married to Irene, Tom becomes the undisputed head of the family during Reconstruction. Targeted by violent Ku Klux Klan night-raiders in North Carolina, Tom organizes and leads a wagon train of his extended family westward to start a new life in Henning, Tennessee.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Female · Adult · Master Weaver & Blacksmith's Wife
characters.overviewBio: An enslaved half-Cherokee weaver on the Murray plantation in Alamance County who marries Tom Murray. Loving, industrious, and steadfast, Irene works alongside Tom to safeguard their children against post-war terrorism and helps establish their new home in Henning, Tennessee.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Female · Elder · Grandmother & Storyteller of Henning
characters.overviewBio: The youngest child of Tom and Irene Murray, born in Alamance County and raised in Henning, Tennessee. Marrying lumber company owner Will Palmer, Cynthia becomes the maternal cornerstone of the family home in Henning. On warm summer evenings on the front porch, Cynthia recites the stories of 'the African' Kunta Kinte, Bell, Kizzy, and Chicken George to her grandson Alex Haley, etching the oral chronicle into his young memory.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Elder · Prosperous Lumber Merchant
characters.overviewBio: Husband of Cynthia Murray and grandfather of Alex Haley. Starting with nothing, Will works tirelessly to buy and build the prosperous W.E. Palmer Lumber Company in Henning, Tennessee, providing financial security and respectability for the extended Kinte descendants.

Daughter of Will and Cynthia Palmer, who attends Lane College, plays piano, and marries professor Simon Alexander Haley. Mother of author Alex Haley, she bridges the family's transition from rural Tennessee into modern education.

characters.archetypeTag: Supporting · Male · Adult · Author, Chronicler & Seventh Generation
characters.overviewBio: Seventh-generation descendant of Kunta Kinte and author of the novel Roots. Inspired by the oral memories passed down on the porch in Henning, Tennessee, Haley embarks on a twelve-year global quest through the British Admiralty archives, slave ship manifests of the Lord Ligonier, and West African villages, finally locating the Kinte clan in Juffure, Gambia, and reuniting the broken lineage.
quotes: In writing this book, I have tried to tell the story of a people—and of a family—that began in Africa and survived the ordeal of slavery.

relationships.notes: Omoro names Kunta under the stars in Juffure and guides him through manhood training into Mandinka warriorhood.
Kunta's memory of his mother's warmth and songs sustains his spirit through the Middle Passage and decades of bondage.
Purchases Kunta in Annapolis, forces the name 'Toby', and sanctions the axing of Kunta's foot after four escape attempts.
Buys Kunta from his brother John, treats his severed foot, and uses him as personal buggy driver for decades.
The elder fiddler nurses Kunta through his maiming, teaches him the plantation reality, and becomes his closest friend.
They marry jumping the broom on the Waller plantation; their union produces Kizzy.
Kunta teaches Kizzy Mandinka words, his clan history, and African drum rhythms, charging her never to forget.
Bell manages Dr. Waller's kitchen with distinction, but he callously rejects her pleas when selling Kizzy.
Upon discovering Kizzy forged a travel pass for Noah, Dr. Waller sells her down south to Tom Lea.
Kizzy writes a fake travel pass to help Noah escape, which precipitates her discovery and sale.
Tom Lea rapes Kizzy upon arrival in North Carolina, impregnating her with George; she detests him.
Kizzy pours Kunta Kinte's stories and the Mandinka words into George's mind throughout his upbringing.
Trains George as his prized gamecock handler, but wagers and loses George to an English lord to cover gambling debts.
Matilda bears eight children with George, remaining faithful through his long exile in England.
George passes the ancestral mantle of leadership to Tom, who leads the post-emancipation generation.
Murray buys Matilda and George's children after Tom Lea's bankruptcy.
Matilda works the Murray plantation alongside her children until Union troops announce freedom.
Tom serves as expert blacksmith for the Murrays, building a reputation for skill and quiet fortitude.
They marry and face down Ku Klux Klan threats, leading their family to Tennessee.
Tom raises Cynthia in Henning, Tennessee, instilling the proud history of Kunta Kinte.
Their marriage establishes the prosperous Palmer home where the oral family history is told.
Passes the oral family stories and educational ambitions down to Bertha.
Cynthia recites the oral saga on the Henning porch to young Alex Haley, inspiring his lifelong quest.
Nurtures Alex's intellect, reading, and writing before her early passing.
Haley traces his lineage across two hundred years back to Kunta Kinte and the village of Juffure.
